To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
prostacyclin biosynthesis by human endothelial progenitor (EPC) cells is a key factor responsible for their proangiogenic function.
prostacyclin (prostaglandin I2) is a key molecule in the control of angiogenic function of human endothelial progenitor (endothelial colony-forming) cells (EPC).
prostacyclin production is an important mechanism of angiogenic function of endothelial precursor cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PGI2 biosynthetic pathway in the control of angiogenic function of EPCS.
the role of prostaglastin production in the regenerative function and angiogenic potential of endothelial progenitors.
the role of prostaglanin biosynthesis in the regenerative function (i.e. the angiogenic capacity) of endothelial progenitors cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prostaglandin pathway, and in particular PGI2, is a critical mediator of angiogenesis in human EPC.
the PGI2 pathway is a novel mechanism of angiogenesis and that the PGI 2 pathway may be a novel therapeutic target for the treatment of ischemic vascular diseases.
PGI2 is an important mediator of the proangiogenic function in EPCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PGI2 biosynthetic pathway plays an important role in the control of the angiogenic function of Epc cells.
the COX-1-derived PGI2 is an important regulator of EPCs angiogenesis.
PGI2 is an important mediator of EPC function, and that this effect is mediated through PPAR†.
The main takeaway from our work is that
prostacyclin biosynthesis is a key mechanism responsible for regenerative function of human endothelial progenitor.
prostacyclin is a key mediator in the control of the angiogenic function of endothelial cells.
PGI2 is an important angiogenic mediator in endothelial progenitor cell function.
